Treaty between the Independent State of Samoa and the Republic of Finland on the Promotion and Protection of Investments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000; International Companies Act 1987, ss. 96 and Schedule 8; Financial Transactions (Proceeds of Crime) Act 2021, as amended; SIFA Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Guidelines (2023); United Nations (Sanctions) Regulations 2018

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised copy of certified passport or national ID of each natural person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or designated notary public of the beneficial owner's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or original bank statement issued within last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or commercial bank in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation and memorandum of association for each corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Commercial bank reference letter confirming identity and standing of the beneficial owner
Certified copy of the Power of Attorney appointing the registered agent and/or trustee company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the power was executed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit's domestic PEP and adverse-media list, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the UK Consolidated Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence is compulsory for PEPs, their family members, and close associates, and for any beneficial owner resident in a jurisdiction identified as high-risk by the Financial Action Task Force. Existing clients must be re-screened at least annually and upon any trigger event, with findings recorded in the UBO register and reported to SIFA where suspicious activity is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) Company Search and Registration Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed names must be submitted in Roman/Latin script. Names in Chinese or other non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into English or Samoan and must include a certified transliteration certificate from an accredited translator. The allowed corporate suffix is 'Limited' or the abbreviation 'Ltd.'. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing company name registered in Samoa, nor may it suggest any connection with the Government of Samoa or any foreign government.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon submission of the name clearance application, the Registrar of International Companies (SIFA) will issue a written decision within 7 business days. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar within 14 days of the notice, explaining why the name should be accepted and proposing any necessary amendments. If rejection is upheld, the applicant may appeal to the Samoa International Financial Authority Appeals Committee within 28 days of the reconsideration decision. The Appeal Committee will decide within 30 days, and its decision may be further challenged by way of judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa. Alternatively, the applicant may file a new name reservation request with a revised proposed name without forfeiting the original application fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are acceptable for internal administrative or marketing functions only. The statutory registered office must be a physical, active office of a licensed registered agent in Samoa, capable of accepting service of process and maintaining required minute books and shareholder registers. The registered agent may provide the physical address; a purely virtual back-office presence is not sufficient for an Employee Stock Ownership Trust administrator.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and preliminary due diligence search fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International Companies Act 1987 Fee Schedule, regulation 7

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation filing fee (minimum capital not required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International Companies Act 1987 and Companies (Fees) Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and registered office service for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing SIFA-licensed market tariff, inclusive of AML/CFT compliance duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register setup and AML/CFT customer due diligence file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended, and SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and/or consular legalization of UBO identity and trust documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, apostille office of the foreign ministry, and/or consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Foreign ministry/consular fee schedules and notarial fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the ESOP Trust declaration and employment incentive plan documents for incorporation pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External corporate counsel / law firm in Samoa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional fee benchmark in Samoa for international company incorporations and ESOP structures

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended), ss. 2, 6-14, 20-24 (incorporation, registered office, capital); Companies Ownership Act 2018 (beneficial ownership filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Office of the Registrar of International Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company, filed together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; an International Company may be incorporated with nil issued capital and shares of no par value. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by the Registrar. Annual license and government fees are payable regardless of issued capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriptions tendered by the founding subscribers are approved, and 1,000 ordinary shares of US$1.00 each are allotted and issued as recorded in the register of members. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, which address is adopted as the address for service. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] is appointed as sole Director and [Secretary Name] as Corporate Secretary, with authority to open and operate bank accounts, execute share certificates, and file all statutory returns. RESOLVED FURTHER, that establishment of the employee stock ownership trust structure, including the share repurchase facility and trustee mandate, is ratified and approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Companies Registry (applications routed through licensed Samoa registered agents)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select two to three permissible corporate names in English ending in 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated' or 'Ltd'. Submit the name reservation request to the licensed agent, who searches the national companies register for identical or confusingly similar names. The approved name is reserved for up to 30 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: List of proposed names in priority order
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused on similarity grounds, submit alternative proposed names. Where refusal is believed erroneous, file a written representation to the Registrar for reconsideration within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent acting under the International Companies Act 1987, s. 7
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The agent drafts the constitutional documents in English, including the name clause, authorized share capital and share classes, director powers, indemnities, and registered agent clause. At least one subscriber executes the documents before a witness; execution is dated and countersigned by the agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend any defective or non-compliant clauses and re-execute the documents with fresh witness signatures. No government stage is engaged at this point, so corrections are made directly between the agent and the subscribers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA - Office of the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the prescribed application for incorporation together with the executed memorandum and articles, and a statutory declaration of compliance signed by the subscribers and the first directors. The registered agent concurrently files its consent to act as registered office holder and the signed consents of the appointed directors and secretary.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act of each director and the secretary
Consent of the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any written requisition or query issued by the Registrar within 14 calendar days, supplying corrected documentation or explanations. A further cure extension may be granted upon written request to the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registration Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA - Office of the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon administrative clearance, pay the registration fee of US$250 and the government stamp duty of US$75 through the licensed agent. The Registrar then issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the corporate registration number, and the company comes into existence as of the certificate date.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued by the Registrar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains any error in the corporate name, date, or registration number, apply for rectification under the International Companies Act 1987. Re-issue is processed upon return of the defective certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance and Beneficial Ownership Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Registrar and licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written board resolution to approve share allotments, adopt the registered office, appoint officers, and ratify the ESOP trust mandate. Maintain the statutory registers at the registered office in Apia and file the beneficial ownership return under the Companies Ownership Act 2018 within 14 days of incorporation.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written minutes
Share certificates and register of members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filing attracts prescribed late fees; cure by filing the overdue or amended return together with a brief explanation statement to the Registrar, and pay the applicable surcharge.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Trust and Company Service Providers Registry (a license is required only where the entity acts as a professional trust service provider to third parties; captive administration of a single employer's employee stock ownership trust is exempt)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - captive employee stock ownership trust administration conducted by an International Company is statutorily exempt from any sectoral operating license under the International Companies Act 1987. Professional trust services to third parties would require authorization under the International Trusts Act 1987 and compliance with Samoa's AML/CFT regime.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - purely administrative and paper-based trust activity with no physical development; no Environmental Impact Assessment or Permit for Minor Development is required under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the trust administration activity. If a leased office is occupied, the company must comply as an ordinary commercial tenant with the Water Resources Management Act 2008 regarding trade waste discharge and with the Waste Management Act 2001 regarding waste segregation, storage, and disposal standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for the leased Apia registered office obtained from the Samoa National Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA); building or occupancy compliance clearance from PUMA; and workplace health and safety compliance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), Ministry of Revenue, Apia, Samoa; online taxpayer portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned entity must first engage a licensed registered agent in Samoa. For an International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987, the certificate of incorporation issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) constitutes the primary tax-exempt charter. The IC must also complete SRA Form TIN-01 to obtain a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN/IRD number) for banking, customs, and employment purposes. The application must be lodged through the registered agent, who verifies the certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director/shareholder particulars, and the agent's practising licence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election is available to a Samoa International Company; the entity is mandatorily exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax on outbound payments under Section 198 of the International Companies Act 1987. If the IC carries on any local non-offshore commercial activity, it may voluntarily register for GST under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2001, but such registration does not affect the corporate income tax exemption.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (Goods and Services Tax / Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (annual taxable turnover threshold for mandatory registration)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance, government API integration, or digital stamping for e-invoices. SRA-accepted invoices may be paper-based or standard electronic invoices; registered persons must file monthly GST returns and remit GST through the SRA online portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated for GST purposes when the goods are exported out of Samoa within 28 days of the date of supply. International services (including offshore administrative services supplied to a non-resident ESOP employer) are zero-rated where the recipient is outside Samoa, the services are performed entirely outside Samoa, and the intellectual or practical benefit of the services does not arise in Samoa. The Samoa International Company tax-exempt status is preserved for the ESOP trust's undisputed offshore revenue; GST zero-rating applies only to any locally registered taxable activities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill with evidence of physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment evidence from the non-resident settlor or employer
Commercial invoice or service contract describing the offshore nature of the ESOP administration services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA may audit any claim of zero-rating for up to 5 years after the annual return is filed. If the exporter fails to substantiate the export or offshore-service supply, the SRA will assess the unpaid GST at 15%, impose a late payment penalty of 20% per annum, and charge monthly interest at the prescribed rate. Fraudulent zero-rating claims attract criminal prosecution under the Revenue Administration Act 2016, fines up to WST 100,000, imprisonment up to 7 years, and full clawback of input tax credits, with personal liability extended to directors and registered agents of the International Company.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) acting pursuant to the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, the Exchange Control Act 2009, and the Exchange Control Regulations 2010.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is a currency subject to exchange control. Current account transactions (trade, services, interest, dividends) are generally permitted for residents / approved non-resident entities subject to documentary verification and Authorized Dealer oversight. Capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, portfolio inflows, loans, guarantees) require the specific approval of the Central Bank of Samoa, unless an express exemption applies. International Companies (ICs) incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 enjoy automatic exchange control approval for transactions involving persons resident outside Samoa, subject to statutory returns and the absence of a Samoan-source business or local beneficial ownership. Profit and capital remittance by an IC to non-residents is free from the usual exchange control application provided the remitting bank verifies the IC's statutory registers and audited or management accounts evidencing available profits or capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 2010, a Samoan exporter is legally obligated to surrender export proceeds through an Authorized Dealer within 30 days of receipt and in accordance with the dealer's notification and conversion instructions; at least 100% of the applicable export proceeds are normally required to be repatriated into Samoa and converted into WST unless a specific exemption is granted. For an International Company not engaged in domestic export trade in Samoa, the surrender rule is not triggered; proceeds for offshore services or trust activities are treated as offshore receipts and may remain in a designated foreign-currency account with an Authorized Dealer or an offshore licensed bank with CBS oversight.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Foreign Currency / WST) and separate Escrow/Trust Account for ESOP contributions
Operational Account and Escrow / Trust Account
Operational Account and Escrow / Trust Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) options are of limited viability for a Samoa International Company. Samoa does not currently issue EMI licenses to pure digital non-bank deposit takers; an offshore EMI would only be permitted to facilitate payments if it holds a banking or money remittance license from the Central Bank of Samoa or operates as a non-deposit-taking remittance agent subject to validation by an Authorized Dealer. Most global EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) do not domicile Samoa entities, and their services may be restricted or impose currency conversion margins. Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. A licensed Samoan commercial bank remains the mandatory anchor for trust/escrow accounts and for maintaining a stable AUD/USD/WST clearing channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of all directors is generally mandated for first-time account opening of International Companies at commercial banks in Samoa. In practice, banks permit a combination of physical attendance by at least one director (or an authorized corporate officer) and remote verification via notarized passports, board resolutions, and a direct video conference with the other directors. A purely paper-based remote opening is not considered acceptable under standard Samoan AML/CFT directives, unless the applicant has an existing relationship with the same banking group in another jurisdiction and that group obtains CBS approval for a remote on-boarding waiver. Directors who are resident in Samoa must appear in person; non-resident directors satisfying rigorous third-party KYC (including e-verification through a licensed corporate service provider) may complete the process largely remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner structure of the ESOP Trust shows individuals unrelated to the company founder or with no verifiable commercial role.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trust deed and dated schedule of beneficiaries; board resolution approving the ESOP plan and trust appointment; full CV and passport of each beneficiary; legal opinion from a licensed Samoa solicitor confirming the legitimate purpose of the trust and the absence of any nominee or concealment arrangement; source of wealth declarations including audited financial statements and tax residence certificates for all substantial beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Funding from a non-bank financial corporation or jurisdiction considered high-risk by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) of Samoa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A source of funds dossier listing the exact correspondent bank and intermediary chain; final-bank confirmation letter; purpose code and contract for the underlying employee incentive arrangement; evidence that the funds originate from the employing company's operational bank account in a FATF / APG member jurisdiction; corporate authorization from the IC's board and copies of the ESOP subscription agreements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained rapid build-up of cash-like balances within the trust escrow account, inconsistent with periodic employee incentive contributions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A full treasury cash flow forecast; the ESOP schedule and valuation report; monthly bank statements showing clear intra- and inter-month matching to employee payroll or equity grants; an independent accountant's letter of no cash-laundering risk; written confirmation that the trust accounts are audited biannually by a Samoan-licensed auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of directors or shareholders from sanction-affected or politically exposed categories without transparent beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP clearance from a recognized compliance database; independent PEP and sanctions screening report; notarized statements of source of wealth; and a legal memorandum from the IC's registered agent confirming compliance with the Samoa International Companies Act 1987 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism Act 2018.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections into the Samoa International Company trust should be routed exclusively via SWIFT-based bank transfers from the parent employer or shareholders to the trust's account at an Authorized Dealer in Samoa. The wire must clearly state a purpose code such as 'Investment into Employee Ownership Trust' or 'Capital Contribution for ESOP Award Funding' in the pending / SWIFT 72Field narrative. Supporting documentation (board resolutions, ESOP plan, subscription agreements) must be lodged with the beneficiary bank prior to the wire, because Samoa banks treat any inward transfer above WST 20,000 or USD 10,000 as a balance-of-payments event. The beneficiary bank must also submit a TEL / balance-of-payments reporting disclosure to the Central Bank of Samoa within five business days. For non-resident funding in USD, AUD, EUR or JPY, the receiving Samoa bank may automatically convert into WST unless the trust has a previously authorized foreign-currency account. If the trust intends to hold and subsequently disburse in the same foreign currency, the trust must obtain an exchange control authorization at account opening (in practice, ICs are summarily approved).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Permitted outbound clearing rails comprise: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct transfers for payroll disbursements to employee bank accounts outside Samoa, using the proper beneficiary bank codes and a narrative for employee compensation (e.g., '/ESOP/ salary / award proceeds'); (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) or Documentary Collection where the ESOP trust purchases equity or settles share transfers through a correspondent bank; (iii) local Samoan NZ clearing or bilateral netting for any on-island employee payments (via BSP or ANZ Samoa's domestic clearing gateway), and (iv) third-party payment aggregators only for small-value recurring awards, provided the aggregator holds an appropriate license in the country of the beneficiary. All outbound transfers above USD 10,000 are subject to CBS reporting and require the trust to provide a tax registration or legal basis verifying the distribution is not a prohibited dividend under the International Companies Act. For equity transfers, the IC must settle via an MT202/COV to a custodian bank outside Samoa, with a completed form confirming the transaction is a transfer of ownership between non-residents and not a sale of Samoan land or property.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FX forwards) with an authorized Samoan dealer, provided the underlying exposure is a genuine commercial payment in WST or foreign currency

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed offshore through a non-Samoan investment bank, referencing the WST/USD or AUD/USD rate, and fully documented as synthetic hedging without any requirement for delivery of WST

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) approved by the Central Bank of Samoa under the exchange control general authorization for international companies, provided the IC provides a board-approved treasury policy
Plain vanilla currency swaps executed with a licensed dealer and registered in the trust's financial management ledger

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty per month; continued failure beyond 12 months exposes the company to administrative strike-off and dissolution. Restoration is available only after payment of arrears and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of International Company Licence / Annual Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies through the Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable with the Annual Return on the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The licence lapses on non-payment; the company is not lawfully in good standing, the registered agent is obligated to notify the Registrar, and the Registrar may strike off the company after 12 months of default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent's Annual Compliance and UBO Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent retained under the International Companies Act 1987
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At or before each anniversary date; thereafter within 30 days of any beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, continued non-confirmation may cause the registered agent to resign, resulting in loss of registered office and subsequent administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit is imposed generally on a Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 1987. A mandatory external audit arises only if the company obtains a licence under Samoa's banking, trust, or insurance legislation, is subject to a consolidation direction from the Financial Services Authority, or if shareholders representing at least 10% of voting rights demand an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) is the de facto reporting benchmark in Samoa for any prepared statutory financial statements; no separate local GAAP is mandated for International Companies. The company may alternatively maintain internally defined accounting records if the board can demonstrate true and fair reflection of transactions.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Registered Agent must obtain written annual confirmation from the board and each beneficial owner verifying the identity, residence, nature of control, and all share transfers completed during the preceding year. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficiary must be recorded in the share register within 14 days and reflected in the next periodic confirmation. Non-compliance triggers mandatory reporting to the Samoa Financial Services Authority by the agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Share Transfer Ledger (where shares are transferred)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $2,500 – $5,000 per annum for a voluntary or regulatory-triggered audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Licensed International Companies (ICs) under the International Companies Act 1987 are exempt from Samoan income tax on all income other than income derived from sources within Samoa, producing a 0% effective tax rate on offshore ESOP administration and trust management fees. No capital gains tax applies. Dividend, interest and royalty payments by an IC to non-residents are outside the Income Tax Act 2015 withholding net. Qualifying financial services entities may also access negotiated tax holiday certification from the Ministry for Revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IC-R1 Annual Return of International Company; lodged with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Apia, through the Samoa International Financial Services Centre (SIFCA) online registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 60 days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation; continued default beyond 90 days triggers strike-off proceedings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company and IC registration number as per the certificate of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact English legal name; append the underlying ESOP trust name in brackets where the IC acts solely as trustee/plan administrator.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and licence number of the Samoan registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent must be a licensed international company service provider; the IC cannot be self-agented.
Provide a physical street address (not a post office box); the address must be the registered agent's office premises in Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital and share class detail.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State number of shares, class, par value and consideration; ESOP trust ICs must identify plan participants holding beneficial interests.
Disclose every natural person with direct or indirect ownership or control of 10% or more; the register is available to the Registrar and Samoan FIU.
Execute statutory declaration confirming no income was derived from sources within Samoa; if Samoan-source income was derived, the IC must instead file Form IR4 with the Ministry for Revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 500; continuation of default beyond 90 days allows Registrar strike-off; the assets of a struck-off IC vest in the Public Trustee and forfeit to the Samoan Government; reinstatement costs WST 2,500 and is unavailable after one year absent proof of legitimate substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IR4 Company Income Tax Return; filed with the Ministry for Revenue, Apia, through the FiliPule electronic filing portal or paper lodgement at Revenue House.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The income year runs 1 January to 31 December; the annual return is due by 30 June of the following year (six months after the income year-end). Provisional tax instalments are payable on dates determined by the Commissioner for Revenue where the IC has Samoan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoan Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and company name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the TIN issued by the Ministry for Revenue upon registration; an IC deriving only foreign-source income is not obliged to have a TIN.
Use ISIC v4 code 6430 (trusts, funds and similar financial entities), mapping to NAICS 2022 code 525920 where a crosswalk is provided.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessable income derived from sources in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Samoan-source income is taxable; foreign-source income of a licensed IC is exempt and must be excluded.
Attach a schedule of foreign-source income relied upon as exempt under the International Companies Act; retain supporting invoices and governing trust documents for 7 years.
Deduct only expenses incurred in producing Samoan-source assessable income; ESOP administration costs attributable to offshore plan participants are not relevant to the Samoan return.
Zero for an IC with no Samoan-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax at the headline rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 27% to taxable income; IC exemption reduces assessable tax to zero where Box 2 is nil.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit and treaty relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits only where a DTA applies and supporting certificates of residence are held; credit is capped at the Samoan tax attributable to that income.
Settle via provisional tax instalments; final balance is due by 30 June following the income year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax schedule (dividends, interest, royalties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report amounts paid to non-residents; licensed ICs report nil where the IC exemption applies to the payments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of WST 200 per month up to a maximum of WST 2,000; late payment surcharge of 5% plus interest at 2% per month on the outstanding balance; failure to register for Samoan-source income attracts a penalty of up to WST 10,000; understatement attracts a 25% shortfall penalty, rising to 200% for intentional evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by a licensed International Company to non-resident shareholders, as the IC is outside the Income Tax Act 2015. The general statutory non-resident dividend withholding tax rate is 15% for dividends paid by a resident (non-IC) company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Samoa maintains a limited double taxation agreement network, principally the Samoa–New Zealand DTA (signed 2012) and tax information exchange arrangements with Australia and other treaty partners. Protocol to invoke relief: (1) the non-resident recipient obtains a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home tax authority; (2) the recipient submits the TRC together with Form WHT-R (Treaty Relief Declaration) to the Samoan paying agent no later than 10 business days before the distribution date; (3) the agent withholds at the reduced treaty rate or applies the IC 0% exemption as applicable; (4) the agent records the relief in the annual withholding schedule attached to Form IR4 and retains the TRC for 7 years; (5) if no TRC is supplied, the statutory 15% is withheld and the beneficiary may file a refund application with the Ministry for Revenue within 3 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding: interest 15%, royalties 15%. For licensed International Companies the IC exemption reduces both to 0% on offshore payments. Under the Samoa–New Zealand DTA, where applicable, interest and royalties are generally reduced to 10% (royalties may be 0% where no right of use arises in Samoa). The 0% IC treatment applies only while the IC is not earning Samoan-source income and remains duly licensed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: WST 1,000,000 aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions; a Samoan Local File and Master File are expected to be maintained once this threshold is exceeded. Thin-capitalisation debt-to-equity safe harbour is set at 1.5:1 for related-party loans.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not enact UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the International Companies Act 1987 and SIFCA supervisory practice impose mandatory substance indicators: a licensed registered agent in Samoa, a physical registered office, board and trustee minutes maintained at the office, a statutory beneficial ownership register, and records evidencing real ESOP plan administration. Absent such substance, the Registrar may strike off the IC and the entity cannot credibly invoke treaty benefits under Samoa's OECD Global Forum commitments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion — Misapplication of the International Company Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately booking Samoan-source commercial, services or property income as 'foreign-source' to exploit the IC 0% exemption; issuing fraudulent invoices for ESOP administration fees with no underlying service; failing to register with the Ministry for Revenue within 30 days of deriving Samoan-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 2012: shortfall penalty of 200% of the evaded tax (minimum WST 5,000); criminal fine up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 years; the Commissioner may reassess for 10 prior income years and issue garnishee orders against Samoan bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the licensed agent who knowingly participate in the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties and interest; the Commissioner may issue a travel prohibition certificate preventing departure from Samoa; upon criminal conviction personal imprisonment applies and the agent's licence is revoked by SIFCA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Abusive Offshore Structuring
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no registered agent, no physical office in Samoa, no beneficial ownership register, and using the ESOP trust solely as an opaque asset shelter; failing to file the IC annual return for two consecutive anniversaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Companies Act 1987: late filing penalty WST 500; strike-off by the Registrar after 90 days of continued default; assets of the struck-off IC vest in the Public Trustee and forfeit to the Samoan Government; reinstatement costs WST 2,500 and is barred after one year unless legitimate substance is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a struck-off IC are personally liable for all debts and obligations incurred after strike-off; the Registrar may disqualify directors from managing any Samoan company for up to 5 years; the facilitating registered agent's licence is suspended and subject to cancellation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Employee Stock Ownership Trust IC without a current beneficial ownership register or customer due diligence files on plan participants and beneficiaries; failing to report suspicious transactions to the Samoan Financial Intelligence Unit; using nominee arrangements to conceal a politically exposed person's interest in the trust.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML/CFT Act 2018: civil penalty up to WST 1,000,000 per continuing breach; SIFCA licence revocation; freezing and forfeiture orders may extend to trust assets; the IC cannot be used to circumvent transaction-reporting thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, trustees and plan administrators are personally subject to the AML/CFT regime; deliberate money-laundering through the trust carries imprisonment up to 10 years and confiscation of trust property and personal assets; travel bans may be imposed at the FIU's request.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Thin Capitalisation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the ESOP trust sponsor or participating employers a non-arm's-length management fee; paying excessive interest on shareholder loans to shift profit offshore; absence of transfer pricing documentation for cross-border related-party transactions exceeding WST 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2015 transfer pricing rules: the Commissioner adjusts the consideration to arm's length, recharacterises debt as equity where the 1.5:1 debt-to-equity safe harbour is breached, and assesses a 25% shortfall penalty plus 2% monthly interest; the general anti-avoidance rule can void the arrangement and extend the reassessment period to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approved the non-arm's-length pricing are jointly assessed for the additional tax; the general anti-avoidance rule makes the scheme void against the Ministry for Revenue; director travel bans and disqualification may follow where the adjustment is concealed.
